stops.title: Pick a lane with nobody pushing
stops.silver: Without the rules of the world you cannot look ahead from a place, so you keep a score for each move from each place, and improving means taking the move with the highest score.
stops.do: The game asks which lane pays more when nothing pushes you: LEFT CLICK for EDGE, RIGHT CLICK for INLAND, MELEE for THE SAME. Then LEFT CLICK or RIGHT CLICK picks your lane, and you walk it with WASD from the white ring to the green ring.
stops.predict: Commit to which lane earns more when every step goes where you aim it.
stops.saw: The edge lane pays 39 and the inland lane 37: each pad costs 1, the goal pays 50, and the edge is two pads shorter. With no randomness, reading off the higher score picks the short way. That is greedy improvement on action values, the step Silver builds his whole loop on.
stops.agent: A plan scored as if every tool call does exactly what was intended looks best when it takes the fewest steps.

stops.title: Lucio arrives: one step in ten
stops.silver: Silver keeps a learner from locking onto its first good guess by making one move in ten a random one, which he calls epsilon-greedy.
stops.do: Lucio now stands inland. The game asks the chance that one step off an edge pad ends over the drop: LEFT CLICK, RIGHT CLICK or MELEE for the three answers. Then pick a lane and walk it.
stops.predict: Commit to how likely a single edge step is to send you over, before you take one.
stops.saw: One step in ten is replaced by a random one of four moves, and one of those four points at the drop, so each edge step falls 1 time in 40. Lucio is the lecture's random move, made for you. Watch the right side: count how many boops you took and where they sent you.
stops.agent: Sampling with some randomness makes a model try other actions now and then, including the ones that cannot be undone.

stops.title: Count the falls along the edge
stops.silver: Silver asks for exploring that never stops but fades, so every move keeps being tried while the learner turns greedy in the end.
stops.do: The game asks how often the whole edge lane ends in a fall with boops on: LEFT CLICK, RIGHT CLICK or MELEE. Then pick a lane and walk it again.
stops.predict: Commit to roughly how many crossings in 100 end over the drop if you always take the edge.
stops.saw: Eleven steps from edge pads at 1 in 40 each gives about 24 falls in 100; counting the walks back after other boops, the game's own arithmetic says about 26. Here the boops never fade, so that cost never shrinks. A schedule that lowers the random share over time, which Silver calls GLIE, is what would let it fall toward zero.
stops.agent: An agent that keeps a fixed amount of randomness pays the same price for it on every run, however much it has learned.

stops.title: Which lane wins in the long run
stops.silver: SARSA updates the score of what you just did toward the reward plus the score of the move you will really make next, random moves included.
stops.do: The game asks which lane earns more on average with boops on: LEFT CLICK for EDGE, RIGHT CLICK for INLAND. The answer and both averages appear, and then you pick a lane for the last crossing and walk it.
stops.predict: Commit to the lane that earns more over many crossings when Lucio is around.
stops.saw: The edge lane averages 0.41 and the inland lane 30.31: a 26 in 100 chance of losing 100 costs far more than two extra pads. These are the scores of the walker who really gets booped, which is what SARSA learns, so SARSA moves inland. Compare your own four returns on the right with those averages.
stops.agent: Score a strategy by the runs the agent actually produces, slips and all, and the cautious route often wins.

stops.title: Name the learner that hugs the edge
stops.silver: Q-learning updates the score of what you did toward the reward plus the best score available where you landed, whatever you do next.
stops.do: The game asks which learner ends up preferring the edge: LEFT CLICK for Q-LEARNING, RIGHT CLICK for SARSA. A short reveal follows on the coach line.
stops.predict: Using lecture 4's rule (move a guess toward the reward plus the next guess), commit to which next guess makes the edge look best.
stops.saw: The best next move is never a boop, so Q-learning scores the edge at 39 and keeps walking it. SARSA counts the boops and scores it 0.41. Q-learning learns about the player you could be while acting as the one you are, which is off-policy; SARSA learns about the one you are, which is on-policy.
stops.agent: Training on what a flawless version would do, while the real agent still slips, is the Q-learning choice.

stops.title: Read the debrief
stops.silver: Silver passes the cliff-walk slide without discussing it; its plot shows the careful learner earning more while it learns and the edge-walking learner falling more.
stops.do: Nothing to press. Read the three debrief lines and your prediction score in the left block; the right block keeps your four crossings and the long-run averages.
stops.predict: Before reading, say to yourself which of your four crossings you would repeat.
stops.saw: You crossed beside a drop under random boops, and the arithmetic showed the short lane losing once the boops were counted. One honest limit: here the boop stands in for your own random move. If the boops belonged to the world itself, Q-learning would learn them too and would also move inland.
stops.agent: Judge a plan by what the agent will really do, mistakes included, not by what a perfect run would score.
